sources.entry: LazyTune - Lightweight menu bar per-app audio mixer and universal media key controller for web browsers and desktop players. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Vic3z/LazyTune) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: LazyTune is a lightweight macOS menu bar app that provides a per-app audio mixer and universal F7/F8/F9 media key control for web browsers and desktop media players.
summary.what_it_does: LazyTune runs as a menu bar popup on macOS and lets you adjust volume, mute, and boost (1x to 4x) for each running app independently. It can route different apps to different output devices or to several devices at once, and it can restore preferred devices and per-app settings on reconnect. Hardware media keys (F7 previous, F8 play/pause, F9 next) control whichever browser tab or native player is currently producing sound, without launching Apple Music. The README lists 103 built-in web media adapters plus an HTML5 fallback, and native control for players such as Spotify, VLC, IINA, and Apple Music. It also offers a now-playing mini-player, global hotkeys, lazytune:// and finetune:// URL schemes for automation, and a 10-band EQ with AutoEQ headphone correction, both lazy-loaded. It auto-pauses playback on headphone unplug or sleep.
use_cases: control volume of individual apps on mac
use media keys with youtube or spotify in a browser
send music to speakers and calls to headphones
automate playback from raycast or alfred
apply headphone eq correction on mac
how_to_run: Download LazyTune.zip from the Releases page and drag LazyTune.app into Applications
If Gatekeeper blocks launch, run: xattr -cr /Applications/LazyTune.app
git clone the repository and cd LazyTune
stack: Swift (implied by macOS app and build scripts)
notable: Universal F7/F8/F9 media keys that target the active player or browser tab and avoid launching Apple Music
Per-app volume with 1x-4x boost plus per-app output routing across multiple devices
Claims about 50 MB RAM and 0% idle CPU, using push notifications instead of AppleScript polling
Lazy-loaded 10-band EQ and 6,000+ AutoEQ headphone profiles that cost nothing until enabled
Forked from FineTune by Ronit Singh; Sparkle update checks removed
caveats: Requires macOS 15.4 or later and Apple Silicon according to the README
Prebuilt app is signed ad-hoc, so Gatekeeper may block first launch and require xattr workaround
Needs Audio Capture and Automation/Apple Events permissions to function fully
